items.t: West Vancouver real estate market stats

faq.a: The wider British Pacific Properties hillside development in the District of West Vancouver — the large-lot benches above Ambleside and Park Royal developed from the early 1930s by Guinness-led British investors, the venture that also built the Lions Gate Bridge; Chartwell, Canterbury and Whitby Estates are enclaves inside it with their own files.

faq.q: Which schools are located in the British Properties?
faq.a: Chartwell Elementary (K–7), 1300 Chartwell Drive, and Sentinel Secondary (Grades 8–12), 1250 Chartwell Drive, sit beside each other on Chartwell Drive inside the area, with Westcot Elementary (760 Westcot Road) at its foot; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the SD45 locator.

faq.q: Are there extra building rules beyond District zoning in the British Properties?
faq.a: Yes. Registered British Properties covenants require British Pacific Properties plan approval before building a new home, extending or altering a building, or erecting a fence or any structure; the covenants differ by subdivision and District bylaws apply in addition.

faq.q: What is being built above the British Properties?
faq.a: Rodgers Creek, under CD3 zoning: Areas 5 and 6 are capped at 354 and 620 homes (974 combined) with apartments up to 16 storeys, and a 354-unit development permit for Area 5 (3900 Cypress Bowl Road) was approved July 8, 2025; Cypress Village initial works proceed under Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties.
